title: Cloudflare Uses an AI Harness to Probe and Harden Its WAF
gist: Cloudflare used frontier AI models inside a Python harness to mutate already-blocked attacks against its WAF; 1,107 attempts across 45 scenarios yielded 49 findings after human triage, mostly SSRF and command injection, and three Managed Ruleset changes.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's AI harness produced 1,107 attempts across 45 scenarios and left 49 findings after human triage, contributing to three Managed Ruleset changes.
insights.speaker: Matt Foster
insights.so_what: AI-driven red-teaming is yielding measurable defensive rule improvements.

insights.claim: Forty-eight of the 49 findings involved command injection or SSRF, leading to new SSRF detections for obfuscated hosts and restricted protocols and an improvement to the SSRF - Cloud rule.
insights.speaker: Matt Foster
insights.so_what: SSRF and command injection encoding evasions are the weakest WAF areas found.

insights.claim: The models were black-box with no access to WAF rules, source code or internal signals, and a Python harness handled request execution, state, and limits while one model proposed mutations and another reviewed responses.
insights.speaker: Matt Foster
insights.so_what: Constraining models inside a deterministic harness makes AI security testing controllable.
insights.locator: A Python harness handled the parts

insights.claim: In an SSRF test the model switched a cloud metadata address from decimal to trailing-dot form and the request got a redirect instead of a block; Cloudflare preserved it for investigation, not as proof of success.
insights.speaker: Matt Foster

insights.claim: Human review stayed the final validation step: checking requests reached the target, stayed malicious, were clearly unblocked, were within WAF scope and reproducible.
insights.speaker: Matt Foster
insights.so_what: Human triage is the throttle on AI-generated false positives.
insights.locator: Human review remained the final validation step

insights.claim: Google Mandiant, OpenAI's Codex Security and Google's PageBreak follow similar discovery-and-validation patterns, with PageBreak validating exploitability so teams are not overwhelmed by plausible unverified findings.
insights.speaker: Matt Foster
insights.so_what: Validation layer, not discovery, is the differentiator for AI security tooling.
insights.quote: the harness around the model: constraining execution, preserving state, validating findings
